chunks: Who keep together what God has ordained held together, and fear their Lord and dread the hardship of the Reckoning,

key_terms.سُوءَ الْحِسَابِ: the hardship or severity of the Reckoning/Accounting

ai.seo_question: What are the key characteristics of the righteous who maintain divine connections?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the concept of 'Wasilat' (means of approach to God), emphasizing that maintaining kinship ties (Silat al-Rahim) is not merely social but a spiritual obligation that strengthens one's connection to the Divine. The mention of fearing 'evil reckoning' (Su' al-Hasab) underscores the Shia emphasis on detailed accountability, where even minor neglect of divine commands can lead to severe consequences, motivating believers to act with both reverence and hope.
